first_row.ref: MISTER QUILTER IS THE APOSTLE OF THE MIDDLE CLASSES AND WE ARE GLAD TO WELCOME HIS GOSPEL
first_row.text: Mr. Quilter is the apostle of the middle classes, and we are glad to welcome his gospel.

last_row.ref: IN FACT HE IS QUITE SEVERE ON MISTER RUSKIN FOR NOT RECOGNISING THAT A PICTURE SHOULD DENOTE THE FRAILTY OF MAN AND REMARKS WITH PLEASING COURTESY AND FELICITOUS GRACE THAT MANY PHASES OF FEELING
last_row.text: In fact, he is quite severe on Mr. Ruskin for not recognizing that a picture should denote the frailty of man, and remarks with pleasing courtesy and felicitous grace that many faces are feeling

clips.ref: MISTER QUILTER IS THE APOSTLE OF THE MIDDLE CLASSES AND WE ARE GLAD TO WELCOME HIS GOSPEL
clips.text: Mr. Quilter is the apostle of the middle classes, and we are glad to welcome his gospel.

clips.ref: NOR IS MISTER QUILTER'S MANNER LESS INTERESTING THAN HIS MATTER
clips.text: Nor is Mr. Quilter's manner less interesting than his matter.

clips.ref: HE TELLS US THAT AT THIS FESTIVE SEASON OF THE YEAR WITH CHRISTMAS AND ROAST BEEF LOOMING BEFORE US SIMILES DRAWN FROM EATING AND ITS RESULTS OCCUR MOST READILY TO THE MIND
clips.text: He tells us that at this festive season of the year, with Christmas and roast beef looming before us, similes drawn from eating and its results occur most readily to the mind.

clips.ref: HE HAS GRAVE DOUBTS WHETHER SIR FREDERICK LEIGHTON'S WORK IS REALLY GREEK AFTER ALL AND CAN DISCOVER IN IT BUT LITTLE OF ROCKY ITHACA
clips.text: He has grave doubts whether Sir Frederick Layton's work is really Greek after all and can discover in it but little of rocky Ithaca.

clips.ref: LINNELL'S PICTURES ARE A SORT OF UP GUARDS AND AT EM PAINTINGS AND MASON'S EXQUISITE IDYLLS ARE AS NATIONAL AS A JINGO POEM MISTER BIRKET FOSTER'S LANDSCAPES SMILE AT ONE MUCH IN THE SAME WAY THAT MISTER CARKER USED TO FLASH HIS TEETH AND MISTER JOHN COLLIER GIVES HIS SITTER A CHEERFUL SLAP ON THE BACK BEFORE HE SAYS LIKE A SHAMPOOER IN A TURKISH BATH NEXT MAN
clips.text: Linnell's pictures are a sort of up-guards-in-item paintings, and Mason's exquisite idles are as national as a jingo poem. Mr. Birkett Foster's landscapes smile at one much in the same way that Mr. Carker used to flash his teeth. And Mr. John Collier gives his sitter a cheerful slap in the back, before he says, like a shampooer and a Turkish bath, next man

clips.ref: IT IS OBVIOUSLY UNNECESSARY FOR US TO POINT OUT HOW LUMINOUS THESE CRITICISMS ARE HOW DELICATE IN EXPRESSION
clips.text: It is obviously unnecessary for us to point out how luminous these criticisms are, how delicate in expression.

clips.ref: ON THE GENERAL PRINCIPLES OF ART MISTER QUILTER WRITES WITH EQUAL LUCIDITY
clips.text: On the general principles of art, Mr. Quilter writes with equal lucidity.

clips.ref: PAINTING HE TELLS US IS OF A DIFFERENT QUALITY TO MATHEMATICS AND FINISH IN ART IS ADDING MORE FACT
clips.text: Painting, he tells us, is of a different quality to mathematics and finish in art is adding more factor.

clips.ref: AS FOR ETCHINGS THEY ARE OF TWO KINDS BRITISH AND FOREIGN
clips.text: as for etchings, there are two kinds, British and foreign.

clips.ref: HE LAMENTS MOST BITTERLY THE DIVORCE THAT HAS BEEN MADE BETWEEN DECORATIVE ART AND WHAT WE USUALLY CALL PICTURES MAKES THE CUSTOMARY APPEAL TO THE LAST JUDGMENT AND REMINDS US THAT IN THE GREAT DAYS OF ART MICHAEL ANGELO WAS THE FURNISHING UPHOLSTERER
clips.text: He limits most bitterly the divorce that has been made between decorative art and what we usually call pictures. Makes a customary appeal to the last judgment and reminds us that in the great days of art Michelangelo was the furnishing upholsterer.
